title: Repository Topology — Ping Identity Demo Platform
description: Architectural assertions about the demo platform codebase: service boundaries, token exchange chain, scope topology, feature flag machinery, RAG stack, compose profiles, and MCP tools. Intended for coding agents to avoid repeated rediscovery.

assertions.claim: The demo banking agents are implemented in demoAgentLangGraphService.js using LangGraph. The agent's system prompt is assembled from a vertical manifest starting at approximately line 1407. This is the sole injection point for grounding context (knowledge grounding or otherwise).

Feature flags follow a three-point wiring pattern: (1) FLAG_REGISTRY in featureFlags.js (~line 33), (2) FIELD_DEFS in configStore.js (~line 152), and optionally (3) QUICK_FLAGS in QuickFlagsPill.js (~line 16) for a header toggle pill. A flag needs all three to be fully operational in the UI.

The RAG stack consists of Weaviate (vector DB), a llama.cpp embedder, and a code chunker/indexer. It is gated by the 'rag' docker-compose profile (docker-compose.yml ~line 840), NOT by a feature flag. There is no ff_* flag for RAG.

The RAG stack powers the Code Explorer page and exposes three MCP tools: code_search, get_code, and list_codebases. These tools are NOT wired into the demo banking agent prompts — the agents get context exclusively from the manifest system prompt.
assertions.source: MCP tool registry, Code Explorer page implementation

citations.ref: MCP tool definitions for code_search, get_code, list_codebases

assertions.claim: Docker-compose profiles gate infrastructure services. The 'rag' profile activates Weaviate + embedder + indexer. Services without a profile run in the default stack. To start RAG: 'docker-compose --profile rag up'. Profiles are an infrastructure decision, distinct from feature flags which are runtime toggles.

Token exchange follows the OAuth 2.0 token exchange grant (RFC 8693). The client presents a subject token to the Ping Identity authorization server, which validates it and issues a new access token with scoped permissions. The gateway enforces token validity before routing to downstream services.
assertions.source: OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange implementation, gateway middleware

assertions.claim: The scope topology defines permission boundaries: 'accounts:read' for balance inquiries, 'accounts:transfer' for initiating transfers, 'admin:config' for configuration changes. Scopes are declared in the authorization server and enforced at the gateway and service level.
assertions.source: Authorization server scope configuration, gateway enforcement

citations.ref: Scope declarations in auth server config

assertions.claim: The gateway acts as the single entry point for all API requests. It performs token validation, scope enforcement, rate limiting, and request routing. Gateway-level flags (distinct from application feature flags) can disable entire routes without code changes.

The configStore (configStore.js) is the persistence layer for all runtime configuration including feature flags. FIELD_DEFS (~line 152) declares the schema for each config field: type, default, label, description, category, and whether changes require restart. Fields with restart:false take effect immediately.

The QuickFlagsPill component renders a row of toggle pills in the application header. Each pill corresponds to an entry in the QUICK_FLAGS array (~line 16). Clicking a pill toggles the associated feature flag in real-time without page reload — designed for live demo toggling by SEs.

Service boundaries: the demo_api_server/ directory contains Express.js services (config, agents, routes). The demo_api_ui/ directory contains the React frontend. Services communicate via internal REST APIs. The LangGraph agent service is the most complex — it orchestrates tool calls, manages conversation state, and assembles prompts.

The graphify-out/ directory stores knowledge bundles — JSON files with .kb.json extension containing deterministic knowledge assertions. Each bundle declares a domain slug and is indexed by the knowledgeLoaderService. The banking-domain bundle grounds the demo agent; the repo-topology bundle describes this codebase for coding agents.

To add a new feature flag: (1) Add entry to FLAG_REGISTRY in featureFlags.js with name, label, description, default, category. (2) Add entry to FIELD_DEFS in configStore.js with type, default, label, description, category, restart. (3) Optionally add to QUICK_FLAGS in QuickFlagsPill.js for header toggle. (4) Read the flag with getFlag('ff_your_flag') in consuming code.
assertions.source: Feature flag pattern across featureFlags.js, configStore.js, QuickFlagsPill.js

assertions.claim: The ff_knowledge_grounding feature flag controls knowledge injection into the demo agent. When ON, knowledgePromptInjector.js appends a <knowledge> block with [K1]-[Kn] assertions after the manifest system prompt. When OFF, the agent uses only the manifest prompt. RAG remains orthogonal — controlled by compose profile, not this flag.

MCP (Model Context Protocol) tools are exposed for AI coding agents. Existing tools: code_search (RAG-powered code search), get_code (retrieve code by path), list_codebases (enumerate indexed repos). The get_knowledge_assertions tool queries knowledge bundles by domain and optional tag filter. MCP tools are distinct from the demo agent's tool-use capabilities.

PingGateway (IG) re-parses /var/gateway/config/mcp-tool-schemas.json on EVERY tools/call, in mcp-request-validation.groovy. If that path is missing or unreadable, IG throws FileNotFoundException and every POST /mcp returns HTTP 500 while docker ps still reports the container healthy; the UI surfaces this only as 'MCP call failed for <tool> (tool_failed)', which looks like a token or policy failure but is not.

Never bind-mount an individual FILE into the PingGateway container on macOS: VirtioFS pins the host inode and git replaces files by rename, so any pull touching it leaves a dangling mount until the container is recreated. mcp-tool-schemas.json is generated to BOTH the repo root (canonical) and ping-gateway/config/, which sits inside a DIRECTORY mount and resolves by name on every open. gen:tool-schemas writes both; toolSchemaDrift.test.ts asserts they stay byte-identical.
